issue.body:
### Description

By default, Keycloak executes *many* SQL statements every three minutes to cleanup expired sessions. With lots of realms, this easily piles up to considerable squandering of resources - even if zero sessions exist!

My proposal would be to first check if there are any sessions in the table at all, and if not, do not rund lots of queries.

Alternatively, check the time of the *first* session the expire and wait *until then*, but do not execute SQL when it simply is not needed.

(On my PostgreSQL 18, a rather unused Keycloak produces 8% CPU load every three minutes)

### Value Proposition

Less resource consumption

### Goals

Much less CPU load when keycloak is "silent"

### Non-Goals

N/A

### Description

Hello! Assume the following case within Keycloak High Availability deployment:
Site A: KC-A, INSPN-A
Site B: KC-B, ISPN-B
And we have this situation: **KC-A is down, INSPN-A is up, KC-B is up, INSPN-B is down**
Is it possible to take the cache from INSPN-A to KC-B and repair the cluster availability? The fact is that KC goes for cashes to the Infinispan that is pointed in KC config as the `KC_CACHE_REMOTE_HOST` variable, and this is the local infinispan "nearby" named INSPN-B, which is down for a some reason. I guess it is impossible to register two infinispan hosts in `KC_CACHE_REMOTE_HOST` variable. KC-B will not go to take caches from INSPN-A, because it does not know about it. May be a possible solution is to specify the INSPN-A host value in `KC_CACHE_REMOTE_HOST` variable in KC-B config, but for some reason it's timeout connection to INSPN is that is located on other cluster:

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

Quarkus distribution tests on Windows occasionally fail because the expected text is missing from the captured error output, while the process has already exited.

Observed on Windows:

- `StartCommandDistTest#failIfOptimizedUsedForFirstFastStartup` receives an empty error output.
- `StartCommandDistTest#testInvalidConfigFileOption` receives only the first line of the error output; the second line (`Try 'kc.bat --help' ...`) is missing.
- `QuarkusPropertiesDistTest#testInvalidSmallRyeKeyStorePathPropertyWin` receives `The DelayedHandler was closed before any children handlers were configured. Messages will be written to stderr.` followed by debug logging instead of the expected `IllegalArgumentException`.

The test harness reads stdout and stderr until the streams are closed and waits for those readers to finish before the assertion, so a plain race between process exit and reading is unlikely to explain this. The failure message of `CLIResult.assertError` shows only the error stream, so it is not visible whether the missing text ended up on stdout or whether the process ended early. The root cause is not known yet.

### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The expected messages are present in the captured error output, or the failure message contains enough information to tell where the output went.

### Actual behavior

The assertion fails and only the error stream is shown.

### How to Reproduce?

The failures are intermittent and have only been seen on Windows runners.

### Anything else?

This is a first step to collect more information; it does not claim to fix the underlying cause.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

storage (persistent user sessions)

### Describe the bug

Since 26.8.0 ([#51851](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/51851) / [#51852](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/51852), commit [d5d5922](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/commit/d5d5922e0eac3770b04bdd977190be6ee8e12b6f)), `UserSessionExpirationLogic` loops over `SESSION_BUCKET_COUNT = 64` buckets. For each bucket, it calls `runInBatches` twice for offline sessions and twice for regular sessions. Every `runInBatches` call runs at least one SELECT in its own transaction, even when the realm has no sessions at all. `BaseExpirationTask` runs `removeExpired` for every realm once per `sessionExpirationPeriod` (180 s by default). As a result, the number of queries grows with realms × 64, whatever the number of sessions.

Per realm and per expiration run (no sessions, Remember Me disabled):

* 26.7.4: **7** SELECTs on `OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`
* 26.8.1: **259** SELECTs (37x). With Remember Me enabled we expect 386, but we have not measured it.

When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled (JDBC tracing is on by default), each SELECT becomes a root span, and each transaction commit becomes a second root trace. So every SELECT produces 3 spans in 2 traces. In deployments with many realms, this shows up as a large, constant increase in database load, trace volume and database audit logs after upgrading to 26.8.

#51851 was about index contention on MSSQL and MySQL. #53211 notes that PostgreSQL benefits less because of its MVCC design. The extra queries, however, are issued on every database.

### Version

26.8.1. The code is the same in 26.8.0, 26.8.2, `release/26.8` and `main` (as of 2026-11-09).

### Regression

- [x] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

When there is nothing to expire, the cost of session expiration should not grow with 64 × the number of realms. It should be comparable to 26.7.x (7 SELECTs per realm per run).

### Actual behavior

Measured with 21 realms (20 empty realms plus master), no sessions, period set to 60 s, over 5 expiration runs:

| Version | SELECTs on OFFLINE_USER_SESSION | Per realm per run | Duration of one run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26.7.4 | 735 | 7 | ~0.2–0.3 s |
| 26.8.1 | 27,195 | 259 | ~6 s |

In 26.8.1, each of the four bucketed queries is called 6,720 times (21 realms × 5 runs × 64 buckets), for example:

```
select ... from OFFLINE_USER_SESSION where REALM_ID=$1 and OFFLINE_FLAG='1' and SESSION_BUCKET=$2 and LAST_SESSION_REFRESH_COARSE<$3 fetch first $4 rows only
```

`BEGIN` was called 27,200 times, which confirms that each SELECT runs in its own transaction.

With `--tracing-enabled=true`, the same window produced 81,595 spans from these three operations:

* `SELECT keycloak.OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`: root span, 27,195
* `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit`: root span, 27,200
* `JtaTransactionWrapper.commit`: child of the commit span, 27,200

### How to Reproduce?

1. Start PostgreSQL 16 with `-c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements -c pg_stat_statements.track=all`, then run `CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements`.
2. Start Keycloak: `kc.sh start-dev --db=postgres --db-url=jdbc:postgresql://<host>/keycloak --db-username=... --db-password=... --spi-user-sessions--infinispan--session-expiration-period=60 --log-level=INFO,org.keycloak.models.sessions.infinispan.expiration:debug`
3. Create 20 empty realms: `kcadm.sh create realms -s realm=r$i -s enabled=true`
4. Wait until one expiration run completes (`PurgeExpired tasks completed` appears in the log), then run `SELECT pg_stat_statements_reset()`.
5. Wait for 5 more runs, then run `SELECT sum(calls) FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE query ILIKE 'select%offline_user_session%'`.
6. Repeat the same steps with 26.7.4 and compare.

### Anything else?

I would like to contribute a fix that keeps the bucket column, the indexes and the bucket count as they are, but queries all buckets in one statement:

* In the four `findExpired*UserSessions*` named queries, change `sess.sessionBucket = :sessionBucket` to `sess.sessionBucket IN (:sessionBuckets)` and pass all bucket values (0..63).
* Call `runInBatches` once per query type instead of once per bucket.

Each batch still runs in its own transaction and is still limited by the batch size, so the transaction scope stays bounded (the concern behind #53296). The near-miss handling and the `hasMore` logic stay as they are. With this change, an empty realm should go back to about 7 SELECTs per run. Before opening the PR, I will compare the execution plans of the current query and the `IN` query on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MSSQL and Oracle with a populated table, to make sure the `IN` version still uses the expiration indexes for the range condition.

The workaround we use for now is to increase `--spi-user-sessions--infinispan--session-expiration-period`.

issue.body:
### Description

Since 26.7 (#48557), `AccountConsole.renderAccountConsole` calls `user.getGroupsCount() > 0` to decide whether to show the Groups tab. On the cached `UserAdapter`, `getGroupsCountByNameContaining` always calls `modelSupplier.get()`, which loads the user from the store, even when the user is fully cached.

Observed on 26.8.1 with a stack trace:

`AccountConsole.getMainPage → renderAccountConsole → UserModel.getGroupsCount() → (cache) UserAdapter.getGroupsCountByNameContaining → UserAdapter.getUserModel() → UserStorageManager.getUserById → provider`

Group membership itself is cached (`CachedUser.groups`), and `getGroupsStream()`, `getGroupsStream(search, first, max)` and `isMemberOf()` use it. Only the count bypasses it.

### Value Proposition

Every Account Console page load costs one external call for users of a non-imported User Storage provider (or one DB query for local users). The provider cannot avoid it, because the cache layer loads the delegate before the provider's own `getGroupsCountByNameContaining` is called.

Fixing this in the cache layer does not only improve the Account Console. It benefits every caller of `UserModel#getGroupsCount()`, including custom applications and extensions (custom providers, authenticators, event listeners, etc.) that rely on the user cache.

### Goals

- For `search == null`, answer `getGroupsCountByNameContaining` from the cached group membership, with the same result as the store (direct memberships, realm groups only, organization groups excluded).
- Add a test showing that a cached user is not reloaded from the provider for the group count.

### Non-Goals

- No change to the semantics of the count or to the name-filtered (`search != null`) path. That path keeps delegating, because the JPA implementation applies admin-permission filters there.
- No change to `AccountConsole`'s visibility logic.

### Discussion

### Notes

- The delegating override was added in 12bc84322a (2020, KEYCLOAK-14974, PR #7387) as part of a large unrelated commit. Neither the commit nor the PR (empty description) gives a reason for it.
- The cost became visible when #48558 added the call on the Account Console page-load path.
- No existing issue or PR found for this.
- Proposed change: a few lines in the cached `UserAdapter.getGroupsCountByNameContaining`, using `getGroupsStream().count()` for `search == null`. This equals the JPA count (direct memberships, `Type.REALM` only) and the `UserModel` default implementation.

issue.body:
### Description

The comments of [CacheManager](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/CacheManager.java)

```java
/*
 * Cache listeners do not receive a @CacheEntryInvalidated event if that node does not have an entry for that item.  So, consider the following.

 1. Node 1 gets current counter for user.  There currently isn't one as this user isn't cached.
 2. Node 1 reads user from DB
 3. Node 2 updates user
 4. Node 2 calls cache.remove(user).  This does not result in an invalidation listener event to node 1!
 5. node 1 checks version counter, checks pass. Stale entry is cached.

 The issue is that Node 1 doesn't have an entry for the user, so it never receives an invalidation listener event from Node 2 thus it can't bump the version.  So, when node 1 goes to cache the user it is stale as the version number was never bumped.

 So how is this issue fixed?  here is pseudo code:

 1. Node 1 calls cacheManager.getCurrentRevision() to get the current local version counter of that User
 2. Node 1 getCurrentRevision() pulls current counter for that user
 3. Node 1 getCurrentRevision() adds a "invalidation.key.userid" to invalidation cache.  Its just a marker. nothing else
 4. Node 2 update user
 5. Node 2 does a cache.remove(user) cache.remove(invalidation.key.userid)
 6. Node 1 receives invalidation event for invalidation.key.userid. Bumps the version counter for that user
 7. node 1 version check fails, it doesn't cache the user
*/
```

In fact, 
```java
/*
 * How is this issue fixed with the current implementation?
 *
 * 1. Node 1 reads a user from the DB and gets the current revision from its local revision cache.
 * 2. Node 2 updates the user, calls invalidateObject(userId), which removes the cache entry and bumps the revision in its local revision cache.
 * 3. Node 2 sends an InvalidationEvent to the cluster.
 * 4. Node 1 receives the InvalidationEvent, calls invalidateObject(userId), and bumps the revision in its own local revision cache.
 * 5. Now, when Node 1 tries to cache or read the user, it checks the revision; if the revision is outdated, the cache is invalidated and not used.
 *
 * This ensures all nodes keep their cache and revision numbers consistent, without using marker keys like "invalidation.key.userid".
 */
```

### Value Proposition

Avoid misleading developers.

### Goals

Provide consistent comments with the implementation.

### Non-Goals

NA

_No response_

26.8.1. The code is the same in 26.8.0, 26.8.2, `release/26.8` and `main` (as of 2026-11-09).

### Regression

- [x] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

When there is nothing to expire, the cost of session expiration should not grow with 64 × the number of realms. It should be comparable to 26.7.x (7 SELECTs per realm per run).

### Actual behavior

Measured with 21 realms (20 empty realms plus master), no sessions, period set to 60 s, over 5 expiration runs:

| Version | SELECTs on OFFLINE_USER_SESSION | Per realm per run | Duration of one run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26.7.4 | 735 | 7 | ~0.2–0.3 s |
| 26.8.1 | 27,195 | 259 | ~6 s |

In 26.8.1, each of the four bucketed queries is called 6,720 times (21 realms × 5 runs × 64 buckets), for example:

```
select ... from OFFLINE_USER_SESSION where REALM_ID=$1 and OFFLINE_FLAG='1' and SESSION_BUCKET=$2 and LAST_SESSION_REFRESH_COARSE<$3 fetch first $4 rows only
```

`BEGIN` was called 27,200 times, which confirms that each SELECT runs in its own transaction.

* `SELECT keycloak.OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`: root span, 27,195
* `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit`: root span, 27,200
* `JtaTransactionWrapper.commit`: child of the commit span, 27,200

2. Start Keycloak: `kc.sh start-dev --db=postgres --db-url=jdbc:postgresql://<host>/keycloak --db-username=... --db-password=... --spi-user-sessions--infinispan--session-expiration-period=60 --log-level=INFO,org.keycloak.models.sessions.infinispan.expiration:debug`
3. Create 20 empty realms: `kcadm.sh create realms -s realm=r$i -s enabled=true`
4. Wait until one expiration run completes (`PurgeExpired tasks completed` appears in the log), then run `SELECT pg_stat_statements_reset()`.

6. Repeat the same steps with 26.7.4 and compare.

### Anything else?

* In the four `findExpired*UserSessions*` named queries, change `sess.sessionBucket = :sessionBucket` to `sess.sessionBucket IN (:sessionBuckets)` and pass all bucket values (0..63).
* Call `runInBatches` once per query type instead of once per bucket.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

`org.keycloak.tests.i18n.LoginPageTest.realmLocalizationMessagesAreNotCachedWithinTheTheme` is flaky in CI. The test saves a realm localization text via Admin API, then immediately opens the login form and asserts the localized text appears in the page source. Intermittently, the login page renders with the default message instead of the realm-specific override.

### Analysis

The Infinispan cache invalidation is **synchronous** — `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit()` commits JPA first, then runs `RealmCacheSession.runInvalidations()` which calls `cache.invalidateObject(id)` (a synchronous local Infinispan remove + version bump). All within one method call on the same thread. The original claim of "async cache invalidation" is incorrect.

The exact root cause of the flakiness is unknown. Investigated and ruled out:
- **Cache invalidation timing**: synchronous within `transactionManager.commit()`, completes before the HTTP response is sent
- **Theme message caching**: `ExtendingTheme.messages` only caches base theme `.properties` files; realm localization texts are always fetched fresh via `getEnhancedMessages(realm, locale)`
- **Browser caching**: login pages have `Cache-Control: no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0`
- **Selenium page load**: WebDriver uses `PageLoadStrategy.NORMAL` (waits for `document.readyState` = "complete")
- **Infinispan revision mechanism**: `addRevisioned()` checks `startupRevision` to prevent stale data from being cached
- **CloseSessionFilter not running**: the known trigger (#51131) is client disconnection (`DiscardRemainingRunner`), which does not apply here — the admin client waits synchronously for the 204 response
- **Clustered cache propagation**: CI uses single-node with `CacheType.LOCAL`

### Idea for a fix

Wrap the assertion in an `Awaitility.await()` retry loop (up to 3 seconds). This is a pragmatic fix that stabilizes the test even though the root cause is not identified.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

_No response_

### Expected behavior

The test should pass reliably. After saving a realm localization text via the Admin API and receiving the response, the next login page request should render with the updated localization.

### Actual behavior

The assertion `assertThat(driver.page().getPageSource(), containsString("Localization Test"))` fails intermittently. The page source contains `<title>Sign in to default</title>` (the default message) instead of the realm localization override.

The test passed on CI retry (attempt 2), confirming it is flaky rather than a persistent failure.

### How to Reproduce?

Run `Forms IT (chrome)` CI job repeatedly. The failure is intermittent and depends on timing.

Example failure: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/36128130358/job/108050340141 (attempt 1 of the run; attempt 2 passed)

Failure output:

```
java.lang.AssertionError:
Expected: a string containing "Localization Test"
     but: was "<html class="login-pf" ...><title>Sign in to default</title>..."
```

The test was originally added for KEYCLOAK-18590.

issue.title: UserCacheSession does not cache the username/email query when the user is already managed in the session

labels.name: user-244ae7c7/repo-234e274a
labels.description: Categorizes a PR related to a bug

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-efda1aec
labels.description: Infinispan — distributed caches, clustering, JGroups, cross-site replication

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

infinispan

### Describe the bug

`UserCacheSession.getUserByUsername()` and `getUserByEmail()` return early when the looked-up user is already in the per-session `managedUsers` map, **before** the `UserListQuery` for the username/email key is stored in the cache. So whenever a user was loaded first by another lookup in the same session, the query for the second key is never cached and every later request pays one delegate lookup for it.

Typical call chain on a warm email login:

1. The login form resolves the user by email (`KeycloakModelUtils.findUserByNameOrEmail` -> `getUserByEmail`). Email query and user come from the cache and the user becomes managed.
2. After authentication the `VERIFY_PROFILE` required action evaluates its trigger on every login. `profile.validate()` runs `DuplicateUsernameValidator`, which calls `session.users().getUserByUsername(realm, username)`.
3. `UserCacheSession.getUserByUsername` finds no cached username query and asks the delegate. The user is already managed, so the method returns `managedUsers.get(userId).user()` and never reaches the block that caches the query.

Since the username query is never stored, step 3 repeats on every login: one `getUserByUsername` call to the user store (an external call for a federation provider; by code reading also a DB query for local JPA users, see "Anything else?"). `VERIFY_PROFILE` is enabled by default for new realms, so this affects the default setup.

The same early return exists in `getUserByFederatedIdentity` and `getServiceAccount`; I'd keep those out of the fix for this issue.

### Version

26.8.1 (code unchanged on main at c5e857e11e)

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

After the first lookup of a user by username, the username query is cached the same way as when the user is not yet managed in the session: with the same `loaded` revision, the lifespan from `getLifespan(...)`, and only if the user is a cached `UserAdapter`. The same applies to the email query. Later logins then need no delegate `getUserByUsername` or `getUserByEmail` call while the user and query entries are valid.

### Actual behavior

The username/email query is only cached when the user is not yet managed in the session. After an email lookup (which manages the user), the username query is never cached, because `getUserByUsername` returns the managed user before reaching the code that caches the query. The same applies in reverse for `getUserByEmail` after a username lookup.

Measured with a federated provider using cache policy `MAX_LIFESPAN`: 0 store calls per warm email login with `VERIFY_PROFILE` disabled, but 1 `getUserByUsername` call per warm email login with it enabled.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create a realm with a user storage provider that counts `getUserByUsername` calls, cache policy `MAX_LIFESPAN`, and `VERIFY_PROFILE` enabled (default).
2. Log in by email once (cold), then log in by email again.
3. Observe the store call count: every email login, including warm ones, triggers one `getUserByUsername` call.
4. Disable `VERIFY_PROFILE`: warm logins make no call.

Alternatively at model level: in one session look up a user by email, then by username; repeat in new sessions. The username query is never cached, so the delegate is called each time.

### Anything else?

### History

- `82ad26189f` (2016, "refactor user cache"): the query was cached unconditionally, before the `managedUsers` check.
- `3e28ac1e46` (2016, "user spi cache policy"): the query caching was moved below `getUserAdapter(...)` to be able to test `adapter instanceof UserAdapter` (don't cache queries for uncached/NO_CACHE users). The `managedUsers` early return stayed above it, which disabled query caching on that path as a side effect. No explanation for this in the commit or later changes.

### Local (JPA) users

By code reading, a cache miss on the username query goes to `UserStorageManager.getUserByAttribute(...)`, which queries the local provider first, so I expect one DB query per warm email login with `VERIFY_PROFILE` enabled. Not yet measured; I'll verify this in the test for the fix.

### Proposed fix

On the managed path, still cache the query if the managed user is a cached `UserAdapter` (and its username/email still matches the lookup key), then return the managed user. Users invalidated in the session, `NO_CACHE`/uncached users and revision checks keep their current behaviour. I intend to provide a PR.

The history analysis, the code reading and the draft of this text were done with Claude Code (AI agent). The federated-provider measurement above is from my own testing. I reviewed and verified the findings before filing.

issue.title: Skip authentication session expiration for realms without authentication sessions

labels.name: user-244ae7c7/repo-b1c5fb21
labels.description: Categorizes a PR related to an enhancement

issue.body:
### Description

The expiration task for JPA-backed authentication sessions queries all 64 session buckets of `ROOT_AUTH_SESSION` for every realm on every expiration run, even when the realm has no authentication sessions at all. With many realms this produces a constant load of up to 64 SELECTs per realm and run on an otherwise idle system. Check with a single index lookup if the realm has any authentication session, and skip the per-bucket queries while the realm is empty.

### Value Proposition

Deployments with many realms that are rarely used no longer issue a constant stream of SELECTs and transactions, which reduces database load, trace volume and database audit log volume. This is the same approach as for the user session expiration in #54886.

### Goals

* When a realm has no root authentication sessions, skip the per-bucket queries and remember the time of that observation.
* Until the authentication session lifespan has passed after that observation, skip the realm without issuing any query. A session created later cannot expire earlier.
* Derive the deadline from the current realm settings on each run, so that changing the lifespan needs no cache invalidation.
* Keep the state in memory on the node that runs the expiration, so that a node without state simply performs the regular check.

### Non-Goals

* No schema or index changes.
* No changes for realms that do have authentication sessions. Skipping individual buckets is tracked separately for user sessions in #55012.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

The bucketed expiration of authentication sessions was introduced in 26.8, so this is not a regression. The expiration is implemented in `AuthenticationSessionExpirationAction`.

* 26.8.1: **259** SELECTs (37x). With Remember Me enabled we expect 386, but we have not measured it.

When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled (JDBC tracing is on by default), each SELECT becomes a root span, and each transaction commit becomes a second root trace. So every SELECT produces 3 spans in 2 traces. In deployments with many realms, this shows up as a large, constant increase in database load, trace volume and database audit logs after upgrading to 26.8.

26.8.1. The code is the same in 26.8.0, 26.8.2, `release/26.8` and `main` (as of 2026-11-09).

- [x] The issue is a regression

| Version | SELECTs on OFFLINE_USER_SESSION | Per realm per run | Duration of one run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26.7.4 | 735 | 7 | ~0.2–0.3 s |
| 26.8.1 | 27,195 | 259 | ~6 s |

In 26.8.1, each of the four bucketed queries is called 6,720 times (21 realms × 5 runs × 64 buckets), for example:

```
select ... from OFFLINE_USER_SESSION where REALM_ID=$1 and OFFLINE_FLAG='1' and SESSION_BUCKET=$2 and LAST_SESSION_REFRESH_COARSE<$3 fetch first $4 rows only
```

`BEGIN` was called 27,200 times, which confirms that each SELECT runs in its own transaction.

With `--tracing-enabled=true`, the same window produced 81,595 spans from these three operations:

* `SELECT keycloak.OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`: root span, 27,195
* `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit`: root span, 27,200
* `JtaTransactionWrapper.commit`: child of the commit span, 27,200

type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
### Description

Currently, the Organizations feature provides excellent multi-tenancy support for managing users, identity providers. However, this multi-tenancy does not extend to OAuth2/OIDC clients. Clients can only be created and managed at the realm level by a realm administrator.

This limitation creates a significant bottleneck in SaaS environments. As a SaaS provider, we want to empower our tenants (Organizations) to self-manage the applications they integrate with our service. For example, a tenant might want to:



Integrate their own internal scripts or services with our APIs using the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow.

Configure a specific OIDC client for their own internal web application.

Manage client secrets and redirect URIs without needing to file a support ticket with us (the realm administrators).

Without this capability, all client management becomes a manual, centralized task that hinders tenant autonomy and scalability.

### Value Proposition

I propose enhancing the Organizations feature to allow organizations to create, configure, and manage their own OAuth2/OIDC clients.

This could be implemented as follows:

A "Clients" Tab in the Organization UI: A new "Clients" section would be added to the organization's administration console, similar to the one at the realm level.

Delegated Permissions: A new set of permissions (e.g., manage-org-clients, view-org-clients) would be created that can be assigned to organization administrators. This would give them the authority to manage clients only within their own organization.

Client Isolation: Clients created by an organization would be scoped to and owned by that organization. A realm administrator would have visibility over all clients, but an organization administrator would only see the clients belonging to their organization.

Policy and Template Control (Optional but ideal): Realm administrators could define policies or client templates that constrain the types of clients an organization can create (e.g., allowed grant types, default scopes, protocol settings).

Example User Story:

As an Administrator of "Company A" (an Organization in Keycloak), I want to register and manage my own OIDC clients so that I can securely connect our internal applications to the main service without relying on the service provider's administrators.

### Goals

The primary goal is to delegate client management to Organization Administrators, enabling true self-service for tenants within a multi-tenant Keycloak deployment. This enhances scalability, autonomy, and security.

Core Capabilities for an Organization Administrator
An Organization Administrator, with the appropriate permissions, should be able to perform the following actions exclusively on clients belonging to their own organization:

1. Full Client CRUD Operations:

Create: Register new OIDC/OAuth2 clients for their organization's applications (web apps, mobile apps, backend services).

Read: View a list of their organization's clients and inspect their configurations.

Update: Modify all standard client settings, such as names, descriptions, and protocol settings.

Delete: Remove clients that are no longer needed.

2. Client Authentication and Authorization Configuration:

Manage Client Secrets: View and regenerate secrets for clients using the client_secret_post or client_secret_basic authentication methods.

Configure Authentication: Set up other authentication methods like JWT with a private key.

Control Grant Types: Enable or disable flows like Authorization Code, Implicit, Client Credentials, etc., for their clients.

Set Redirect URIs: Manage the list of allowed redirect_uri patterns for their applications to ensure secure authentication flows.

3. Scope and Role Management:

Assign Scopes: Attach realm roles and client roles (from other clients) to their client's scope.

Manage Service Accounts: If a client has a service account, manage the roles assigned to that service account.

4. User Interface Integration:

Dedicated "Clients" Tab: Access all these capabilities through a new "Clients" section within their organization's view in the Keycloak Admin Console. The UI should be isolated, showing only their organization's clients.

### Non-Goals

To maintain realm security, stability, and clear separation of duties, this feature should not provide the following capabilities to Organization Administrators. These responsibilities must remain with the Realm Administrators.

1. No Management of Realm-Level Resources:

Realm Roles: Organization Administrators should not be able to create, edit, or delete realm-level roles. They can only assign existing, approved realm roles to their client scopes.

Authentication Flows: They cannot create, copy, or modify any authentication, registration, or reset-credential flows for the realm. These flows define the fundamental security posture of the entire realm.

Realm-Level Identity Providers: They cannot create or configure new Identity Providers for the entire realm. They can only use the IdPs that a Realm Administrator has explicitly enabled for their organization.

2. No Creation of Shared, Cross-Organization Resources:

Client Scopes: Organization Administrators should not be able to create new "Shared Client Scopes" that would be visible or usable by other organizations. They can only configure the scope for their own clients using predefined roles and mappers.

Protocol Mappers: They cannot create new protocol mappers or modify built-in ones. The ability to add custom mappers (especially script mappers) is a high-privilege operation and must remain with the Realm Administrator.

3. No Control Over Realm-Wide Policies and Security:

Client Policies: Organization Administrators are subject to Client Policies but cannot create, view, or modify them. This ensures the Realm Administrator can enforce security standards (e.g., token settings, required grant types) across all organizations.

Realm Keys: They will have no access to the realm's token signing keys or other cryptographic settings.

Token Lifespan: They cannot override the realm's default token lifespan settings. This must be controlled centrally by the Realm Administrator.

4. No "Escape" from Organizational Boundaries:

An administrator for "Organization A" must never be able to view, modify, or manage clients belonging to "Organization B" or clients that have no organization assigned. All actions must be strictly confined within their own organizational container.

issue.body:
### Description

Given an authentication request with the scope "openid organization", the organization claim is not added to the access token when using transient users. 

Steps to reproduce:

- Enable the transient user feature
- Configure a first realm acting as an identity provider
- Create a user in this realm
- Configure a second realm acting as a broker of identity
- Set the first realm as an IdP of the broker realm.
- Add an organization to the broker realm and link the Idp
- Disable "do not store user" to enable persistent user setting for the Idp of the broker realm.
- Authenticate against the broker realm with a scope "openid organization"

=> The organization claim is inserted in the access token.

- Enable "do not store user" to enable transient user setting for the Idp of the broker realm and remove the user previously stored.
- Authenticate against the broker realm with a scope "openid organization"

=> The organization claim is not inserted in the access token.



### Discussion

_No response_

### Motivation

The transient users feature is extremely useful for the identity brokering.
The organization feature is useful to scale when the number of IdP (tenant) is large by avoiding or mixing the 1 realm per tenant pattern.
Not having the claim organization in the access token prevents us from using the organization feature and the transient user feature at the same time as we cannot easily identify the tenant (the organization).

### Details

_No response_

issue.body:
### Description

As a follow-up to the ID-JAG (Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant) initial support (#49005), Keycloak should advertise its support for the ID-JAG profile in its authorization server metadata.

Section 7.2 of draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-06 defines the `authorization_grant_profiles_supported` metadata parameter. A Resource Authorization Server that supports ID-JAG indicates this by including `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag` in that parameter.

This is not only a draft-level nice-to-have. The MCP **Enterprise-Managed Authorization** extension (protocol revision 2026-07-28, stable), Section 6 "Discovery", relies on exactly this mechanism: an MCP Client determines whether a Resource Authorization Server supports the profile by checking for `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag` in `authorization_grant_profiles_supported`.

https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/blob/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization/2026-07-28/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx#6-discovery

Without this metadata, MCP Clients cannot discover that a Keycloak realm acting as the MCP Server's authorization server supports Enterprise-Managed Authorization, even though the grant itself is already implemented.

### Value Proposition

- Enables Keycloak to be used as a Resource Authorization Server for MCP Servers under the MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension, with standard discovery.
- Allows MCP Clients (and other ID-JAG clients) to detect support automatically instead of relying on out-of-band configuration.
- Completes the resource-side ID-JAG implementation in line with the latest draft.

### Goals

- Add `authorization_grant_profiles_supported` to the realm's OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) and OpenID Provider Metadata (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`).
- Include `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-profile:id-jag` when the ID-JAG feature (`identity-assertion-jwt`) is enabled. Per Section 7.2, this indicates only that the server implements the ID-JAG processing rules, not that any particular issuer will be accepted.
- Ensure `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` is included in `grant_types_supported` whenever the ID-JAG profile is advertised, as required by Section 7.2.
- Omit the parameter (or the value) when the feature is disabled.
- Add tests for the metadata output.

### Non-Goals

- Changes to ID-JAG issuance (IdP side / token exchange), including IdP Authorization Server metadata (`identity_chaining_requested_token_types_supported`, `id_jag_signing_alg_values_supported`, Section 7.1).
- Disclosing trusted issuers or other issuer-specific trust relationships in metadata (Section 9.7 prohibits using `authorization_grant_profiles_supported` for this).
- Other parts of the MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension.


### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

- draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-06, Section 7.2:
  https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant-06.html#section-7.2
- Related: #49005 (ID-JAG: initial support)

labels.name: user-244ae7c7/repo-b1c5fb21
labels.description: Categorizes a PR related to an enhancement

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-9d506d64
labels.description: SCIM — user and group provisioning, filtered search, PATCH operations

labels.name: user-c64ca2e7/repo-b1763e2d
labels.description: Issue type or area was assigned automatically by the triage bot

issue.body:
### Description

The SCIM API lets realm administrators expose custom attributes on the **User** resource. They map User Profile attributes to custom extension schemas with the `kc.scim.schema.attribute` annotation. The **Group** resource has no equivalent. Its model is fixed to `displayName`, `externalId`, `members` and `meta.*` (`GroupCoreModelSchema#getModelAttributeNames` returns `Set.of("name", "externalId", "members")`).

Group attributes cannot be exposed under a custom SCIM extension schema, and custom group extension schemas are not listed by the `/Schemas` endpoint.

This request is to let administrators map Keycloak group attributes to attributes in a custom SCIM Group extension schema, in the same way as for users.

### Value Proposition

Groups are commonly synchronized from an external directory. SCIM clients need a stable identifier or other directory metadata on each group, for example an LDAP `entryUUID`.

- For users this works today: map the LDAP attribute to a User Profile attribute and annotate it for SCIM.
- For groups the only supported slot is `externalId`. The built-in LDAP group mapper copies each "Mapped Group Attributes" entry under its **LDAP attribute name**, so the value never reaches `externalId`. Administrators have to run a post-sync script through the Admin API to copy it, and rerun it after every group sync.
- Any other group metadata a SCIM consumer needs cannot be exposed at all.

Supporting group extension attributes would remove the need for these workarounds and make Group behaviour consistent with User.

### Goals

- Allow an administrator to map a Keycloak group attribute to an attribute in a custom SCIM Group extension schema, for example `urn:example:params:scim:schemas:extension:custom:1.0:Group:<attribute>`.
- Return the extension values in Group responses under the extension schema URN, and add the URN to the resource's `schemas` array.
- List configured Group extension schemas in `/Schemas`, and only when at least one attribute is mapped, as for users.
- Support reading, creating and updating mapped attributes through SCIM, and filtering on them using the full schema URI prefix.
- Respect the existing read-only semantics, so that attributes which should not be changed by SCIM clients (for example values synchronized from LDAP) can be marked as such.
- Validate configuration the way User Profile mappings are validated today, for example rejecting duplicate SCIM mappings.

### Non-Goals

- Changing the core Group schema or the semantics of `displayName`, `members` or `externalId`.
- Introducing a full declarative "Group Profile" with validators and permissions comparable to User Profile.
- Changing how the LDAP group mapper imports attributes. A separate enhancement could add a rename or target-attribute option, but it is not required here.
- Supporting extension attributes on resource types other than Group.
- Supporting complex or multivalued sub-attribute structures beyond what is already supported for user extensions, in the first iteration.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

Observed behaviour, checked against `26.6.7`. I also read the source of the `26.8.1` tag and `main`: the group schema still lists only `name`, `externalId` and `members`, and no group extension class exists. I did not test 26.8 on a running server.

Reference points in the code:

- User extension support: `UserExtensionModelSchema`, `AbstractUserModelSchema#ANNOTATION_SCIM_SCHEMA_ATTRIBUTE`, `UPConfigUtils` SCIM validation.
- Group schema: `scim/model/.../group/GroupCoreModelSchema.java`.
- Docs: the SCIM guide describes extensions as a User Profile feature, and `managing-groups.adoc` documents `externalId` as the only group attribute mapping.

Current workaround for the `entryUUID` case:

1. Add the LDAP attribute to "Mapped Group Attributes" on the group LDAP mapper.
2. After each group sync, copy that group attribute to `externalId` through `PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/groups/{id}`. The endpoint replaces the full attribute map, so the script has to send back every existing attribute.

labels.name: user-244ae7c7/repo-b1c5fb21

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-efde29d2

labels.name: user-c64ca2e7/repo-b1763e2d
labels.description: Issue type or area was assigned automatically by the triage bot

issue.body:
### Description

When a realm has no active key for a requested algorithm and use, `DefaultKeyManager` asks the key provider factories to create a fallback key. The first factory whose `createFallbackKeys()` returns `true` generates a software key and stores it as a new key provider component (`fallback-<algorithm>`, priority -100). There is no way to turn this off.

In deployments where all signing keys must come from a hardware security module or an external KMS through a custom key provider, this means that a key provider that is temporarily unavailable, or a client configured with an algorithm the HSM does not provide, makes Keycloak silently generate and use a software key. Because the fallback key is persisted, it stays in the realm and in the JWKS even after the HSM provider is back, until an administrator removes it.

The only workaround we found is a custom `KeyProviderFactory` whose `createFallbackKeys()` throws. That depends on the iteration order of the factories, which is not defined.

### Value Proposition

Operators who require hardware-backed keys can make Keycloak fail closed: the request fails instead of a token being signed with a key that was generated in software without anyone noticing.

### Goals

- A server-wide option to disable fallback key generation, e.g. `--spi-keys--generate-fallback-keys=false`. The default stays `true`.
- When it is disabled and no active key is available, the request fails, and the log names the realm, algorithm and use.
- Document the fallback behaviour and the option in the Server Administration Guide.

### Non-Goals

- Changing the default behaviour.
- A per-realm setting. It could be added later on top of the server-wide option if there is demand.
- Any HSM or PKCS#11 integration.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

I'm happy to provide the PR. A server-wide option fits the use case, as the requirement to use hardware-backed keys usually applies to the whole deployment, and it needs no admin console or data model changes. New realms get their default key providers created explicitly, so disabling the fallback does not affect realm creation.

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

storage (persistent user sessions)

### Describe the bug

Since 26.8.0 ([#51851](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/51851) / [#51852](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/51852), commit [d5d5922](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/commit/d5d5922e0eac3770b04bdd977190be6ee8e12b6f)), `UserSessionExpirationLogic` loops over `SESSION_BUCKET_COUNT = 64` buckets. For each bucket, it calls `runInBatches` twice for offline sessions and twice for regular sessions. Every `runInBatches` call runs at least one SELECT in its own transaction, even when the realm has no sessions at all. `BaseExpirationTask` runs `removeExpired` for every realm once per `sessionExpirationPeriod` (180 s by default). As a result, the number of queries grows with realms × 64, whatever the number of sessions.

Per realm and per expiration run (no sessions, Remember Me disabled):

* 26.7.4: **7** SELECTs on `OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`
* 26.8.1: **259** SELECTs (37x). With Remember Me enabled we expect 386, but we have not measured it.

When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled (JDBC tracing is on by default), each SELECT becomes a root span, and each transaction commit becomes a second root trace. So every SELECT produces 3 spans in 2 traces. In deployments with many realms, this shows up as a large, constant increase in database load, trace volume and database audit logs after upgrading to 26.8.

#51851 was about index contention on MSSQL and MySQL. #53211 notes that PostgreSQL benefits less because of its MVCC design. The extra queries, however, are issued on every database.

### Version

26.8.1. The code is the same in 26.8.0, 26.8.2, `release/26.8` and `main` (as of 2026-11-09).

### Regression

- [x] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

When there is nothing to expire, the cost of session expiration should not grow with 64 × the number of realms. It should be comparable to 26.7.x (7 SELECTs per realm per run).

### Actual behavior

Measured with 21 realms (20 empty realms plus master), no sessions, period set to 60 s, over 5 expiration runs:

| Version | SELECTs on OFFLINE_USER_SESSION | Per realm per run | Duration of one run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26.7.4 | 735 | 7 | ~0.2–0.3 s |
| 26.8.1 | 27,195 | 259 | ~6 s |

In 26.8.1, each of the four bucketed queries is called 6,720 times (21 realms × 5 runs × 64 buckets), for example:

```
select ... from OFFLINE_USER_SESSION where REALM_ID=$1 and OFFLINE_FLAG='1' and SESSION_BUCKET=$2 and LAST_SESSION_REFRESH_COARSE<$3 fetch first $4 rows only
```

`BEGIN` was called 27,200 times, which confirms that each SELECT runs in its own transaction.

With `--tracing-enabled=true`, the same window produced 81,595 spans from these three operations:

* `SELECT keycloak.OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`: root span, 27,195
* `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit`: root span, 27,200
* `JtaTransactionWrapper.commit`: child of the commit span, 27,200

### How to Reproduce?

1. Start PostgreSQL 16 with `-c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements -c pg_stat_statements.track=all`, then run `CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements`.
2. Start Keycloak: `kc.sh start-dev --db=postgres --db-url=jdbc:postgresql://<host>/keycloak --db-username=... --db-password=... --spi-user-sessions--infinispan--session-expiration-period=60 --log-level=INFO,org.keycloak.models.sessions.infinispan.expiration:debug`
3. Create 20 empty realms: `kcadm.sh create realms -s realm=r$i -s enabled=true`
4. Wait until one expiration run completes (`PurgeExpired tasks completed` appears in the log), then run `SELECT pg_stat_statements_reset()`.
5. Wait for 5 more runs, then run `SELECT sum(calls) FROM pg_stat_statements WHERE query ILIKE 'select%offline_user_session%'`.
6. Repeat the same steps with 26.7.4 and compare.

### Anything else?

I would like to contribute a fix that keeps the bucket column, the indexes and the bucket count as they are, but queries all buckets in one statement:

* In the four `findExpired*UserSessions*` named queries, change `sess.sessionBucket = :sessionBucket` to `sess.sessionBucket IN (:sessionBuckets)` and pass all bucket values (0..63).
* Call `runInBatches` once per query type instead of once per bucket.

Each batch still runs in its own transaction and is still limited by the batch size, so the transaction scope stays bounded (the concern behind #53296). The near-miss handling and the `hasMore` logic stay as they are. With this change, an empty realm should go back to about 7 SELECTs per run. Before opening the PR, I will compare the execution plans of the current query and the `IN` query on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MSSQL and Oracle with a populated table, to make sure the `IN` version still uses the expiration indexes for the range condition.

The workaround we use for now is to increase `--spi-user-sessions--infinispan--session-expiration-period`.

labels.description: Issue type or area was assigned automatically by the triage bot

issue.body:
### Description

A client secret can change as a side effect of `PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}`:

- the `secret-rotation` client policy executor generates a new secret because the current one has expired,
- client authentication is switched off and back on,
- the payload carries a different `secret`.

In all three cases the only admin event is the generic `UPDATE` on `clients/{id}`, identical to an update that left the secret untouched. Only the regenerate endpoint (`POST .../client-secret`) emits an event of its own (`ACTION` on `clients/{id}/client-secret`).

### Value Proposition

Event listeners and audit trails cannot tell from admin events that a client's secret changed. They have to keep their own record of the secret state and compare it on every client update.

Client secret rotation is a supported feature since 26.8, so a rotation triggered by an unrelated update is now a regular case, and it is the one where the admin did not ask for a new secret.

### Goals

- Every client update that changes the client secret is recognizable as such from the admin events.
- A listener can detect a secret change with one rule, whatever caused it.
- The secret value is not exposed in the event.
- Updates that do not change the secret produce the same events as today.

### Non-Goals

- Secret changes outside the Admin REST API: realm import, partial import, dynamic client registration.

### Discussion

_No response_

### Notes

Three ways this could look:

1. **Same event as the regenerate endpoint**: an additional `ACTION` on `clients/{id}/client-secret` after the `UPDATE`.
   - Listeners need one rule, and existing consumers of that event get the new cases for free.
   - Two events per request, and the resource path names an endpoint that was not called.
2. **A new, dedicated event** for a secret change.
   - Unambiguous.
   - Needs a new resource type or path convention, and the regenerate endpoint keeps its own shape unless it changes too.
3. **A detail on the existing `UPDATE` event.**
   - One event per request, no new types, and nothing changes for consumers that ignore details.
   - Same approach as the user `UPDATE` event, which carries `previous_enabled` / `updated_enabled` details since 26.8 so that listeners can tell a disabled account from any other update.
   - Listeners need two rules, unless the regenerate event carries the same detail.

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

storage (persistent user sessions)

### Describe the bug

Since 26.8.0 ([#51851](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/51851) / [#51852](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/51852), commit [d5d5922](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/commit/d5d5922e0eac3770b04bdd977190be6ee8e12b6f)), `UserSessionExpirationLogic` loops over `SESSION_BUCKET_COUNT = 64` buckets. For each bucket, it calls `runInBatches` twice for offline sessions and twice for regular sessions. Every `runInBatches` call runs at least one SELECT in its own transaction, even when the realm has no sessions at all. `BaseExpirationTask` runs `removeExpired` for every realm once per `sessionExpirationPeriod` (180 s by default). As a result, the number of queries grows with realms × 64, whatever the number of sessions.

Per realm and per expiration run (no sessions, Remember Me disabled):

* 26.7.4: **7** SELECTs on `OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`
* 26.8.1: **259** SELECTs (37x). With Remember Me enabled we expect 386, but we have not measured it.

When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled (JDBC tracing is on by default), each SELECT becomes a root span, and each transaction commit becomes a second root trace. So every SELECT produces 3 spans in 2 traces. In deployments with many realms, this shows up as a large, constant increase in database load, trace volume and database audit logs after upgrading to 26.8.

#51851 was about index contention on MSSQL and MySQL. #53211 notes that PostgreSQL benefits less because of its MVCC design. The extra queries, however, are issued on every database.

### Version

26.8.1. The code is the same in 26.8.0, 26.8.2, `release/26.8` and `main` (as of 2026-11-09).

### Regression

- [x] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

When there is nothing to expire, the cost of session expiration should not grow with 64 × the number of realms. It should be comparable to 26.7.x (7 SELECTs per realm per run).

### Actual behavior

Measured with 21 realms (20 empty realms plus master), no sessions, period set to 60 s, over 5 expiration runs:

| Version | SELECTs on OFFLINE_USER_SESSION | Per realm per run | Duration of one run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26.7.4 | 735 | 7 | ~0.2–0.3 s |
| 26.8.1 | 27,195 | 259 | ~6 s |

In 26.8.1, each of the four bucketed queries is called 6,720 times (21 realms × 5 runs × 64 buckets), for example:

```
select ... from OFFLINE_USER_SESSION where REALM_ID=$1 and OFFLINE_FLAG='1' and SESSION_BUCKET=$2 and LAST_SESSION_REFRESH_COARSE<$3 fetch first $4 rows only
```

`BEGIN` was called 27,200 times, which confirms that each SELECT runs in its own transaction.

With `--tracing-enabled=true`, the same window produced 81,595 spans from these three operations:

* `SELECT keycloak.OFFLINE_USER_SESSION`: root span, 27,195
* `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit`: root span, 27,200
* `JtaTransactionWrapper.commit`: child of the commit span, 27,200

### How to Reproduce?

1. Start PostgreSQL 16 with `-c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements -c pg_stat_statements.track=all`, then run `CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements`.
2. Start Keycloak: `kc.sh start-dev --db=postgres --db-url=jdbc:postgresql://<host>/keycloak --db-username=... --db-password=... --spi-user-sessions--infinispan--session-expiration-period=60 --log-level=INFO,org.keycloak.models.sessions.infinispan.expiration:debug`
3. Create 20 empty realms: `kcadm.sh create realms -s realm=r$i -s enabled=true`

### Area

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

`org.keycloak.tests.i18n.LoginPageTest.realmLocalizationMessagesAreNotCachedWithinTheTheme` is flaky in CI. The test saves a realm localization text via Admin API, then immediately opens the login form and asserts the localized text appears in the page source. Intermittently, the login page renders with the default message instead of the realm-specific override.

### Analysis

The Infinispan cache invalidation is **synchronous** — `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit()` commits JPA first, then runs `RealmCacheSession.runInvalidations()` which calls `cache.invalidateObject(id)` (a synchronous local Infinispan remove + version bump). All within one method call on the same thread. The original claim of "async cache invalidation" is incorrect.

The exact root cause of the flakiness is unknown. Investigated and ruled out:
- **Cache invalidation timing**: synchronous within `transactionManager.commit()`, completes before the HTTP response is sent
- **Theme message caching**: `ExtendingTheme.messages` only caches base theme `.properties` files; realm localization texts are always fetched fresh via `getEnhancedMessages(realm, locale)`
- **Browser caching**: login pages have `Cache-Control: no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0`
- **Selenium page load**: WebDriver uses `PageLoadStrategy.NORMAL` (waits for `document.readyState` = "complete")
- **Infinispan revision mechanism**: `addRevisioned()` checks `startupRevision` to prevent stale data from being cached
- **CloseSessionFilter not running**: the known trigger (#51131) is client disconnection (`DiscardRemainingRunner`), which does not apply here — the admin client waits synchronously for the 204 response
- **Clustered cache propagation**: CI uses single-node with `CacheType.LOCAL`

### Idea for a fix

Wrap the assertion in an `Awaitility.await()` retry loop (up to 3 seconds). This is a pragmatic fix that stabilizes the test even though the root cause is not identified.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

_No response_

### Expected behavior

The test should pass reliably. After saving a realm localization text via the Admin API and receiving the response, the next login page request should render with the updated localization.

### Actual behavior

The assertion `assertThat(driver.page().getPageSource(), containsString("Localization Test"))` fails intermittently. The page source contains `<title>Sign in to default</title>` (the default message) instead of the realm localization override.

The test passed on CI retry (attempt 2), confirming it is flaky rather than a persistent failure.

### How to Reproduce?

Run `Forms IT (chrome)` CI job repeatedly. The failure is intermittent and depends on timing.

Example failure: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/36128130358/job/108050340141 (attempt 1 of the run; attempt 2 passed)

### Anything else?

Failure output:

```
java.lang.AssertionError:
Expected: a string containing "Localization Test"
     but: was "<html class="login-pf" ...><title>Sign in to default</title>..."
```

The test was originally added for KEYCLOAK-18590.

issue.title: Stabilize localization message test
issue.body:
Closes #53310

The Admin API's realm cache invalidation runs in `afterTransaction.commit()`, which can complete after the HTTP response reaches the client. A test that immediately loads the login page after saving a localization text can therefore hit a stale cache entry. This is a test-level timing issue, not a server bug — the cache converges within milliseconds.

Polling with Awaitility (3 s cap) was chosen over a fixed sleep because it self-adjusts: fast when the cache invalidates promptly, only retries on the rare occasion it doesn't. A server-side fix (moving invalidation before the response) would be disproportionate for a sub-millisecond race that only affects back-to-back Admin API + rendering calls.

Both the save and delete paths are wrapped, since the same race applies in both directions.

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

`WindowsServiceDistTest.testServiceLifecycle` fails intermittently in the Windows Quarkus integration tests with `Service should be in STOPPED state ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>`. The service was installed and started, and Keycloak was reachable. After `net stop` the service stayed in `STOP_PENDING` for longer than the 60 seconds the test waits. The whole test took about 170 seconds, compared to about 84 seconds in successful runs. The cleanup of the test then failed with `The service cannot accept control messages at this time` as the service was still stopping.

The service is installed with Apache Commons Daemon Procrun in `exe` mode, with `kc.bat start` as start image and `kc.bat stop` as stop image (`StopTimeout` defaults to 30 seconds). There is no `stop` command in `kc.bat` or in the Keycloak CLI, so the stop image only starts a JVM that prints an unknown command error. Nothing signals the running Keycloak process to shut down.

Procrun then waits for `kc.bat` to exit for the stop timeout. As `kc.bat` exits only when its `java` child exits, this is expected to always run into the timeout. Afterwards Procrun terminates the process tree using `TerminateProcess`, which does not run JVM shutdown hooks. Every stop therefore takes at least the stop timeout and ends with a forced kill, and how long the termination takes depends on the runner. In the failing run, the stop took more than the 60 seconds the test waits for.

The test only verifies the state of the service and that the HTTP port is closed, and not that the Keycloak process has exited or has shut down gracefully.

### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The service reaches the `STOPPED` state in a timely manner after `net stop`, and the test fails with information on why if it doesn't.

### Actual behavior

The stop takes at least the stop timeout, as the stop image does not stop Keycloak, and Procrun then terminates the process tree. On a slow runner this exceeded the time the test waits.

### How to Reproduce?

The failure is intermittent in CI on `windows-latest`: run `WindowsServiceDistTest` repeatedly.

### Anything else?

The documentation of the Windows service lists `StopParams: stop` as a setting that is applied, and describes `--stop-timeout` as the time to wait for the service to stop gracefully.

issue.body:
## Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

## Area

ci

## Describe the bug

CI test jobs ("Base IT", "Forms IT") fail intermittently with Maven dependency resolution errors for `org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine:5.10.3`. The artifact is not in the weekly Maven cache because it is neither a declared dependency nor a transitive dependency of any declared dependency — it is auto-provisioned by the Surefire plugin at test runtime when it detects `junit-jupiter-api` on the classpath.

When Maven Central is rate-limiting GitHub Actions runners (403 Forbidden) or experiencing connectivity issues (Connection reset), Surefire's attempt to download `junit-jupiter-engine` at test execution time fails, causing the entire test job to fail.

This is the same class of issue as #52327, where `surefire-junit-platform` was also not in the cache because it is auto-detected rather than declared.

## Version

main (nightly)

## Expected behavior

CI test jobs should not depend on Maven Central availability at test execution time. All required artifacts should be pre-downloaded into the weekly Maven cache during the Build job.

## Actual behavior

Test jobs fail with errors like:

```
Could not resolve dependencies for project org.keycloak.testsuite:integration-arquillian-tests-base:jar:999.0.0-SNAPSHOT:
  Failed to collect dependencies at org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine:jar:5.10.3:
    Could not transfer artifact org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine:jar:5.10.3 from/to central:
      status code: 403, reason phrase: Forbidden
```

## How to Reproduce?

This is a transient failure that depends on Maven Central rate-limiting. Examples:
- https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/34597188859/job/103257068671 (Base IT job)
- https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/34597188859/job/103257068847 (Forms IT job)

## Anything else?

Root cause: `junit-vintage-engine:5.10.3` and `junit-jupiter-api:5.10.3` are declared as compile-scope dependencies in `testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/pom.xml`. However, `junit-jupiter-engine` is a **sibling** engine, not a transitive dependency of either. Surefire auto-provisions it at test runtime when it finds `junit-jupiter-api` on the classpath. Since it is not a declared or transitive dependency, `dependency:resolve` in the Build job does not download it, and it is missing from the weekly cache.

### Before reporting an issue

- [X] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

Tests using `@InjectTimeOffSet(enableForCaches = true)` of the new test framework can fail with a cascading error when a time offset request does not complete cleanly.

When the offset is reset at the end of a test, the client sends `set(0)` to the server. For `enableForCaches = true`, the server-side `TimeOffSetRealmResourceProvider` treats every offset that is not greater than zero as a request to call `InfinispanTimeUtil.disableTestingTimeService(...)`. This method throws `IllegalStateException: Calling revertTimeService when testing TimeService was not set` when the testing time service was not enabled before, and the client then receives a `500 Internal Server Error`.

The testing time service is not enabled, for example, when the earlier request that should have enabled it failed on the way (such as `NoHttpResponseException: localhost:8080 failed to respond`) but the client already recorded the new offset and therefore resets it in the cleanup. The cleanup error is then reported as a suppressed exception of the original failure and hides what happened.

Observed with `org.keycloak.tests.forms.LoginTest#loginRememberMeExpiredMaxLifespan`, followed by failures of other tests in the same class.

### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Resetting the time offset to `0` succeeds, regardless of whether the testing time service for the caches had been enabled before. The original failure is not accompanied by a failing cleanup.

### Actual behavior

The server logs `Uncaught server error: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Calling revertTimeService when testing TimeService was not set` and responds with a 500 to the reset of the offset.

### How to Reproduce?

Run a test with `@InjectTimeOffSet(enableForCaches = true)` where `TimeOffSet.set(...)` is called with a positive value but the testing time service was never enabled on the server (for example because that request failed), and let the test finish. The cleanup calls `set(0)`, which fails with a 500.

### Anything else?

`InfinispanTimeUtil.disableTestingTimeService(KeycloakSession)` lives in `test-framework/remote-providers`.

The user table renders its empty state on its first render, as the loading state of the table starts as `false`, and then replaces it with a spinner once loading starts. The helper then waits for `add-user` until the test timeout, although the page shows the empty state again as soon as the users have been loaded.

### Version

main

### Expected behavior

The helper clicks the button that creates a user, independent of which of the two buttons is shown and independent of intermediate loading states.

### Actual behavior

The test fails with a timeout when the empty state is replaced by the loading spinner between the two checks in the helper.

### How to Reproduce?

The failure is intermittent. It needs the realm to have no users and the Users page to be opened while the helper's two checks happen across the initial render and the start of loading.

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

`org.keycloak.tests.i18n.LoginPageTest.realmLocalizationMessagesAreNotCachedWithinTheTheme` is flaky in CI. The test saves a realm localization text via Admin API, then immediately opens the login form and asserts the localized text appears in the page source. Intermittently, the login page renders with the default message instead of the realm-specific override.

### Analysis

The Infinispan cache invalidation is **synchronous** — `DefaultKeycloakTransactionManager.commit()` commits JPA first, then runs `RealmCacheSession.runInvalidations()` which calls `cache.invalidateObject(id)` (a synchronous local Infinispan remove + version bump). All within one method call on the same thread. The original claim of "async cache invalidation" is incorrect.

The exact root cause of the flakiness is unknown. Investigated and ruled out:
- **Cache invalidation timing**: synchronous within `transactionManager.commit()`, completes before the HTTP response is sent
- **Theme message caching**: `ExtendingTheme.messages` only caches base theme `.properties` files; realm localization texts are always fetched fresh via `getEnhancedMessages(realm, locale)`
- **Browser caching**: login pages have `Cache-Control: no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0`
- **Selenium page load**: WebDriver uses `PageLoadStrategy.NORMAL` (waits for `document.readyState` = "complete")
- **Infinispan revision mechanism**: `addRevisioned()` checks `startupRevision` to prevent stale data from being cached
- **CloseSessionFilter not running**: the known trigger (#51131) is client disconnection (`DiscardRemainingRunner`), which does not apply here — the admin client waits synchronously for the 204 response
- **Clustered cache propagation**: CI uses single-node with `CacheType.LOCAL`

### Idea for a fix

Wrap the assertion in an `Awaitility.await()` retry loop (up to 3 seconds). This is a pragmatic fix that stabilizes the test even though the root cause is not identified.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

_No response_

### Expected behavior

The test should pass reliably. After saving a realm localization text via the Admin API and receiving the response, the next login page request should render with the updated localization.

### Actual behavior

The assertion `assertThat(driver.page().getPageSource(), containsString("Localization Test"))` fails intermittently. The page source contains `<title>Sign in to default</title>` (the default message) instead of the realm localization override.

The test passed on CI retry (attempt 2), confirming it is flaky rather than a persistent failure.

### How to Reproduce?

Run `Forms IT (chrome)` CI job repeatedly. The failure is intermittent and depends on timing.

Example failure: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/36128130358/job/108050340141 (attempt 1 of the run; attempt 2 passed)

### Anything else?

Failure output:

```
java.lang.AssertionError:
Expected: a string containing "Localization Test"
     but: was "<html class="login-pf" ...><title>Sign in to default</title>..."
```

### Description

`OIDCIdentityProvider` stores the nonce it sends to the upstream IdP under the constant `BROKER_NONCE_PARAM` (`"BROKER_NONCE"`), both as an authentication-session client note and in the `BrokeredIdentityContext` context data. Custom OIDC-based identity providers (subclasses of `OIDCIdentityProvider`) can reuse Keycloak's nonce handling without copying an internal string literal that could silently diverge in a future release.

_No response_

issue.title: Resolve Antora example$ Kroki diagram targets and show placeholders for diagrams that cannot render (#516)
issue.body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?
- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Other, please describe:

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
- [x] No
- [ ] Yes

## Checklist:
- [x] I have updated the [documentation](https://github.com/asciidoctor/asciidoctor-intellij-plugin/blob/main/doc/users-guide/modules/ROOT/pages/features/) to reflect the changes introduced by this PR.

Second and last part after #2111; together they replace #2054.

## The authoring contract this implements

- **Pages** reference a diagram source by Antora resource id: `plantuml::example$order-model.puml[]`. The id stays in AsciiDoc, where every consumer has the module context.
- **Diagram sources** (`.puml`) include each other with plain relative PlantUML includes: `!include ../../layout/colors.puml`, `!includesub ./roles.puml!Core`. No Antora syntax inside PlantUML, so every `.puml` stays a valid standalone diagram for the PlantUML CLI or the PlantUML integration plugin.

This is how the Antora site renders with the asciidoctor-kroki JavaScript extension, and (with a small Antora extension) how the Antora PDF export works. The include inlining of #2054, which taught the plugin to resolve `example$` ids *inside* PlantUML, is therefore not carried over: the 2.0 preprocessor from #2111 resolves the relative includes against the resolved diagram file.

## What

- `AntoraReferenceAdapter.resolveAntoraResourcePath` (from #2054): resolve an Antora resource id to a local path within the current module, reusing the plugin's existing Antora resolution.
- `kroki-antora.rb`: prepends `resolve_target_path(parent, target)` so `plantuml::example$x.puml[]` resolves inside an Antora module. Nothing else.
- `kroki-placeholder.rb`: instead of an error paragraph, a broken image, or a silently degraded diagram, the preview shows a placeholder box naming the diagram type and the reason, with an **Open <file>** link that opens the diagram source in the IDE editor (where the PlantUML integration plugin, if installed, previews it). Triggers: unreadable target; a local `!include` still present after preprocessing (missing file: the Kroki server would drop the line and render the rest); a `kroki-error` block from the Kroki extension. Ruby-only on purpose: the browser fetches the image, so a transport failure (server unreachable) still shows as a broken image, as before. The document attribute `kroki-preview-placeholder` shows placeholders for all Kroki diagrams without contacting the server.
- Users guide and changelog.

## Tests

`AsciiDocWrapperTest`, among them:
- `testShouldResolveAntoraExampleResourceId` on the existing `antoraModule` fixture.
- `testShouldRenderAntoraExampleDiagramViaKroki`: a temp Antora module written to disk and registered as a content root; `plantuml::example$model.puml[]` with a relative include and `example$nested/deep/nested.puml` with `!include ../../layout.puml` render (Kroki URL decoded, included text present); an unresolvable target, a missing include file and `kroki-preview-placeholder` each yield a placeholder.

## Try it

Demo repo: https://github.com/cachescrubber/antora-kroki-example (`main`), page `docs/modules/ROOT/pages/index.adoc`. All five macro diagrams render with the shared layout; rename `examples/layout/colors.puml` and only the affected diagrams become placeholders naming the missing include. Comparison: the release plugin renders the same page without the layout.

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- The opt-out is a document attribute rather than a settings checkbox (adding a setting touches the settings form and every constructor call site).
- An inline `[plantuml]` block has no file to open, so its placeholder shows the diagram text instead.

Reviewed beforehand in cachescrubber/asciidoctor-intellij-plugin#2.

Refs #516. Supersedes #2054 together with #2111.

issue.title: Test framework runs cleanups in registration order instead of reverse order

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-5b7aea37
labels.description: Test suites — flaky/failing tests, CI test config, test migration

labels.name: user-244ae7c7/repo-234e274a

labels.name: user-3ef72433/repo-007038bc

issue.body:
### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

The test framework runs the registered cleanup tasks of `ManagedRealm`, `ManagedClient`, `ManagedUser` and `ManagedOrganization` in the order they were added (`cleanupTasks.forEach(...)`) instead of in reverse order. When a test registers more than one cleanup that touches the same resource, the cleanup registered last is applied last, so it leaves behind the intermediate state instead of the original state.

### Version

main (nightly)

### Expected behavior

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

operator

### Describe the bug

The "Test OLM installation" job of the Operator CI workflow intermittently fails in the step "Arrange OLM test installation" when `docker push` to the Minikube registry fails with `Get "http://192.168.49.2:5000/v2/": dial tcp 192.168.49.2:5000: connect: connection refused`. Example: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/40720821918/job/122933332643

The job starts Minikube with `--addons=registry` and immediately afterwards builds the Keycloak image and pushes it to `$(minikube ip):5000` in `operator/scripts/olm-testing.sh`. `minikube start` can return before the registry addon accepts connections on port 5000, so the push races with the addon start. The follow-up failure `error: the server doesn't have a resource type "keycloaks"` in the "Debug Custom Resources" step is only a consequence, as the operator was never installed.

Fix: add a step to the job that waits until the registry pod is ready and answers on `http://$(minikube ip):5000/v2/` before the images are pushed.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The job waits for the registry and passes reliably.

### Actual behavior

```
+ docker push 192.168.49.2:5000/ca8bafkeycloak:86400000.0.0
The push refers to repository [192.168.49.2:5000/ca8bafkeycloak]
Get "http://192.168.49.2:5000/v2/": dial tcp 192.168.49.2:5000: connect: connection refused
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

### How to Reproduce?

The failure happens only sporadically in CI, depending on how fast the registry addon becomes ready.

### Anything else?

The Minikube registry addon is used in the Operator CI workflow on `main`, `release/26.8`, `release/26.6` and `release/26.4`.
