labels.name: user-244ae7c7/repo-234e274a
labels.description: Categorizes a PR related to a bug

labels.description: Must be worked on very soon

labels.description: Quarkus distribution — packaging, container images, server config (kc.sh)

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

[`KeycloakProcessor.configureDefaultPersistenceUnitEntities()`](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/quarkus/deployment/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/deployment/KeycloakProcessor.java#L666) calls `descriptor.addClasses()` which mutates a shared `ArrayList` inside `ParsedPersistenceXmlDescriptor`. At the same time, Quarkus's [`HibernateOrmProcessor.contributePersistenceXmlToJpaModel()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L456-L465) iterates that same list - it passes `descriptor.getManagedClassNames()` to [`new JpaModelPersistenceUnitContributionBuildItem()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/JpaModelPersistenceUnitContributionBuildItem.java#L25) whose constructor calls `new TreeSet<>(explicitlyListedClassNames)`. Both steps run in parallel with no ordering between them than can cause `ConcurrentModificationException`.

The race window is narrow (1 write vs iterating ~64 items), but recent Quarkus changes (quarkusio/quarkus#53087, quarkusio/quarkus#53086, quarkusio/quarkus#53084) altered build step scheduling enough to [expose it on CI](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/23222979491/job/67500088174). Fails during re-augmentation in `LDAPUserLoginTest`.
In order to fix it on our end, we could try to stop mutating the shared descriptor. Instead of `descriptor.addClasses(targetName)`, we cancollect the additional entities and produce a separate `JpaModelPersistenceUnitContributionBuildItem`. This follows the same pattern Quarkus itself uses - [`contributePersistenceXmlToJpaModel()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L455-L465) and [`contributeClasspathScanningToJpaModel()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L467-L479) both produce this build item instead of mutating the descriptor. The descriptor stays immutable after creation, eliminating the race.

It's difficult to reproduce it reliably within our standard testsuite, so I tried to create a reproducer for the sake of demonstration. I also tested a fix, heavily inspired by Quarkus approach mentioned above. Both can be found [here](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/compare/main...Pepo48:keycloak:fix-cme).

It's also important to mention that we plan to [deprecate persistence.xml](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/41464) and that the CME failure hasn't been spotted in `quarkus-next` since then.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Without possible race condition.

### Actual behavior

Race condition possible, albeit race window is very small.

### How to Reproduce?

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/commit/2043c40e384a9ac4eeae160512166103afc6d985

### Anything else?

issue.body:
### Area

testsuite

### Describe the bug

The test framework runs the registered cleanup tasks of `ManagedRealm`, `ManagedClient`, `ManagedUser` and `ManagedOrganization` in the order they were added (`cleanupTasks.forEach(...)`) instead of in reverse order. When a test registers more than one cleanup that touches the same resource, the cleanup registered last is applied last, so it leaves behind the intermediate state instead of the original state.

### Version

main (nightly)

### Expected behavior

Cleanups are unwound in reverse order (last registered, first executed), so the resource ends up in the state it had before the test, and dependent changes are undone before the changes they depend on.

### Actual behavior

Cleanups run in registration order. For example, calling `realm.updateClientWithCleanup("my-client", ...)` twice in one test for the same client registers two restore tasks. The first restores the original client, the second then re-applies the state after the first update, so the changes of the first update stay in place for subsequent tests.

### How to Reproduce?

1. In a test, call `realm.updateClientWithCleanup("some-client", c -> c.attribute("attr-a", "x"))`.
2. In the same test, call `realm.updateClientWithCleanup("some-client", c -> c.attribute("attr-b", "y"))`.
3. After the test, the cleanups run in the order `original`, then `state after the first update`, so `attr-a` is still set to `x` in the next test.

### Anything else?

Found while reviewing the CI failures of #53876.
No test in the repository is known to fail today because of the ordering, as the existing tests that call the cleanup methods more than once don't touch the same resource twice.
There are roughly 567 usages of `cleanup().add(...)` that need to be checked for a dependency on the current order before changing it.

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

ci

### Describe the bug

The Windows CI build intermittently fails when the `generate:openapi` step of `js/libs/keycloak-admin-client` cannot download the Kiota binary from the GitHub releases of `microsoft/kiota`. Example: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/40709149518/attempts/1?pr=54408

The step runs `kiota generate ...`, which resolves to the `kiota` bin of the npm package `@kiota-community/kiota-gen`, not to Microsoft's executable. This wrapper downloads `https://github.com/microsoft/kiota/releases/download/v1.32.4/<os>-<arch>.zip` into `js/libs/keycloak-admin-client/.kiota` on every run unless `.kiota/<version>/kiota` already exists. In version 1.0.2 the existence check ignored the `.exe` suffix on Windows, so a cached binary would never have been found and the download happened on every Windows run. It is also not covered by the PNPM store cache, as the binary is not part of the PNPM store, and it was not cached by any other step. Wireit's GitHub Actions caching is disabled on Windows as well, so nothing avoided the download.

Upstream fixed the Windows check in `kiota-community/kiota-js-extra` (https://github.com/kiota-community/kiota-js-extra/pull/14, released in `@kiota-community/kiota-gen` 1.0.3).

Fix: upgrade to `@kiota-community/kiota-gen` 1.0.3 and cache the `.kiota` directory in the `pnpm-store-cache` composite action, keyed by the OS and the pinned `KIOTA_VERSION`.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The Kiota binary is downloaded once and then restored from the CI cache on all operating systems, so a temporary failure to download from GitHub releases doesn't fail the build.

### Actual behavior

The download of the Kiota binary fails and the build fails with it.

### How to Reproduce?

The failure happens only sporadically in CI when downloading from GitHub releases fails.

### Anything else?

The Kiota-based client generation is present on `main`, `release/26.8` and `release/26.6`, but not on `release/26.4`.

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

dist/quarkus

### Describe the bug

[`KeycloakProcessor.configureDefaultPersistenceUnitEntities()`](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/quarkus/deployment/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/deployment/KeycloakProcessor.java#L666) calls `descriptor.addClasses()` which mutates a shared `ArrayList` inside `ParsedPersistenceXmlDescriptor`. At the same time, Quarkus's [`HibernateOrmProcessor.contributePersistenceXmlToJpaModel()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L456-L465) iterates that same list - it passes `descriptor.getManagedClassNames()` to [`new JpaModelPersistenceUnitContributionBuildItem()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/JpaModelPersistenceUnitContributionBuildItem.java#L25) whose constructor calls `new TreeSet<>(explicitlyListedClassNames)`. Both steps run in parallel with no ordering between them than can cause `ConcurrentModificationException`.

The race window is narrow (1 write vs iterating ~64 items), but recent Quarkus changes (quarkusio/quarkus#53087, quarkusio/quarkus#53086, quarkusio/quarkus#53084) altered build step scheduling enough to [expose it on CI](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/actions/runs/23222979491/job/67500088174). Fails during re-augmentation in `LDAPUserLoginTest`.
In order to fix it on our end, we could try to stop mutating the shared descriptor. Instead of `descriptor.addClasses(targetName)`, we cancollect the additional entities and produce a separate `JpaModelPersistenceUnitContributionBuildItem`. This follows the same pattern Quarkus itself uses - [`contributePersistenceXmlToJpaModel()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L455-L465) and [`contributeClasspathScanningToJpaModel()`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/hibernate-orm/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/deployment/HibernateOrmProcessor.java#L467-L479) both produce this build item instead of mutating the descriptor. The descriptor stays immutable after creation, eliminating the race.

It's difficult to reproduce it reliably within our standard testsuite, so I tried to create a reproducer for the sake of demonstration. I also tested a fix, heavily inspired by Quarkus approach mentioned above. Both can be found [here](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/compare/main...Pepo48:keycloak:fix-cme).

It's also important to mention that we plan to [deprecate persistence.xml](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/41464) and that the CME failure hasn't been spotted in `quarkus-next` since then.

### Version

nightly

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Without possible race condition.

### Actual behavior

Race condition possible, albeit race window is very small.

### How to Reproduce?

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/commit/2043c40e384a9ac4eeae160512166103afc6d985

### Anything else?

_No response_

issue.body:
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

infinispan

### Describe the bug

In a 2-node Keycloak cluster, a realm update made through the Admin Console is persisted and visible on one node, but the other node keeps serving the previous realm representation. The divergence does not resolve on its own: it lasted more than 2.5 minutes, and was only fixed by restarting the stale node.

The cluster is healthy: both nodes report the same cluster view, and no WARN or ERROR about cache or invalidation appears in the logs.

## Version

Keycloak 26.8.1 (also observed on 26.7.4 before the upgrade). The image bundles Infinispan 16.0.15 (per the image contents; please correct if inaccurate).

## Environment

- 2 Keycloak nodes on AWS ECS Fargate, one task per node, behind an Application Load Balancer. Each task runs a reverse proxy sidecar that forwards to the local Keycloak.
- PostgreSQL (RDS), KC_CACHE=ispn, custom cache configuration file with JDBC_PING discovery.
- Realm cache is a local cache (realms); the work cache is replicated-cache.
- Options: --db=postgres --cache=ispn --health-enabled=true --metrics-enabled=true



### Version

26.8.1 et 26.7.4

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

After the save, every read returns the new displayName, on both nodes, within a short time.

### Actual behavior

Responses are split between the two nodes. Node A returns the new value (5210 bytes, which includes the 7 added bytes). Node B returns the old value (5203 bytes) for at least 2 min 30 s after the save, across several reads. Node B never received the invalidation. Restarting node B makes it return the new value.

The save was processed by node A, and reads from the Admin Console session were also served by node A.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Start two nodes in the same cluster. Confirm both are members of the same view in the logs (ISPN000094).
2. Read GET /admin/realms/<realm> six times in a row through the load balancer and note the displayName.
3. In the Admin Console, change the realm display name (for example, append " (test)") and save.
4. Read GET /admin/realms/<realm> six times in a row through the load balancer, and log the response size of each call.
5. Wait 2 to 3 minutes and repeat step 4.

### Anything else?

- The same behavior appeared for a change made with the Keycloak Terraform provider: the first apply reported success, the next reads showed the old value, and a second apply was needed.
- No ERROR or WARN about cache or invalidation at default log level. Invalidation events are probably visible at DEBUG for org.keycloak.models.cache and org.infinispan. Debug logs for a reproduction can be provided.
- This looks related to #33731, #25837 and #45966, but is not identical.
